title: The Essentialist
coreMove: Make the hidden cost of capable overcommitment visible, then replace scattered availability with a filter for highest contribution.
sourcePressure: The chapter introduces the Essentialist versus Nonessentialist contrast, the paradox that success creates options that erode clarity, and the three truths: choice, few things matter, and doing anything is not doing everything.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would write a generic introduction about being productive, simplifying life, or trying harder to prioritize.

tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds...
make a list of priorities without a trade-off
generic say no to one thing today

exampleSpecs.domain: rural trauma surgeon after a regional award brings three new committees
exampleSpecs.audience: surgeon whose success has attracted civic requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: patient readiness and teaching rounds are displaced by prestige invitations
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She places the award plaque beside the trauma-call board and circles the one committee that directly improves rural response time.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An award plaque leans against a trauma-call board.

exampleSpecs.domain: regional bird-rescue director after a viral release video triples volunteer offers
exampleSpecs.audience: nonprofit leader whose success has created attractive noise
exampleSpecs.stakes: new volunteer energy can either protect injured birds or become tour management
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He pins the intake chart above the media request stack and redirects volunteers to transport shifts before accepting interviews.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A feather intake chart sits on a stack of interview requests.

exampleSpecs.domain: independent board-game designer after a convention hit attracts licensing requests
exampleSpecs.audience: creator tempted to chase every post-success opportunity
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next prototype may die under meetings that look like growth
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She sets the prototype deck beside three licensing envelopes and says yes only to the partner who can improve playtesting.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A prototype deck sits beside three licensing envelopes.

exampleSpecs.domain: public defender invited onto every courthouse reform task force
exampleSpecs.audience: advocate whose competence makes every reform group want her
exampleSpecs.stakes: case preparation for current clients can vanish under worthy committees
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before, every task force gets a yes; after, she marks only the bail-hearing group that changes next week’s docket.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A docket calendar is covered by task-force badges.

exampleSpecs.domain: community radio engineer after the station wins a local journalism prize
exampleSpecs.audience: technical lead whose prize attracts expansion requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: the transmitter maintenance that earned trust may be neglected
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He finds the dead-air log under the award program and writes the filter: protect signal reliability before new shows.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A dead-air log is tucked under an award program.

exampleSpecs.domain: artisan bakery whose croissants made a national list
exampleSpecs.audience: owner pulled from craft into wholesale offers
exampleSpecs.stakes: the signature bake may weaken under sudden scale
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She predicts wholesale will prove success, then checks the laminated bake schedule and rejects orders that would change the morning mix.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A laminated bake schedule rests under wholesale order forms.

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one request that arrived because you have succeeded. Put it beside the work success should protect, then write the filter that decides whether it belongs.
